title: Proof run
meaning: One CI run of every test suite at one exact commit, with an outcome for every automated test record, attested by the provider's trusted signer.

title: Test outcome
meaning: What one test record's test did in a proof run: passed, failed or skipped, with why when it did not pass.

title: Attestation
meaning: A signed statement about one commit, kept by the CI provider, that names its signer and predicate type; STEGO's evidence is attestations, never files committed back.

title: Ratchet
meaning: The change gate's rule: no obligation that was designed, built or proved at the base head may lose that standing; new obligations may arrive unproved.

title: Gate
meaning: A judgement of one commit that CI enforces: the change gate on each pull request, and the release gate before a release is published.

title: Base head
meaning: The commit at the head of the branch a change asks to merge into, which the change gate measures against.

title: Proof ledger
meaning: The view of what a commit proved, built from verified attestations alone: each test record with its result there and the last commit it passed at.

title: Share
meaning: A coverage count over the total, such as proved over all obligations; the three shares are designed, built and proved.

title: Module cache
meaning: The module zips one source revision needs, recorded by digest, which builds use with the network off.

title: Build record
meaning: The record of one build: every input by digest, the build settings, and the executable and SBOMs it produced.

title: Bit-identical rebuild
meaning: A second build from the same source revision, Go SDK and module cache that gives the same bytes as the first.

title: SBOM
meaning: A software bill of materials: the list of every module in an executable, in SPDX or CycloneDX.

title: Keyless signature
meaning: A cosign signature made with a short-lived certificate for the signer's OIDC identity, recorded in a public transparency log, with no long-lived key.

title: Pinned reusable workflow
meaning: The platform's CI workflow, at one exact reference, that every service's pipeline calls; its identity is the only one that may sign images.

title: Declaration
meaning: The one file that states what a service is. An agent writes it, and it is the only input STEGO accepts for a service.

title: Entity
meaning: A data shape a declaration names, with fields and their constraints and no access pattern.

title: Collection
meaning: An access pattern over one entity: its scope, its operations and its path.

title: Slot binding
meaning: A place where a service binds its own rules, as fills, to a slot a component declares.

title: Fault
meaning: One way a declaration breaks a rule, given as structured data an agent can act on.

title: Experimental acceptance
meaning: A statement in a declaration that it accepts a component that is not ga, until a date.

title: Tenant
meaning: One organisation the service serves. Its identifier comes from a verified identity claim. Every request path runs with one tenant set.

title: Tenant kind
meaning: What an entity states about tenants: owned, shared or system. owned rows belong to one tenant; shared rows are read by all and written by system; system rows have no tenant and are never exposed through a tenant request.

title: Sensitivity
meaning: What a field states about its content: public, pii or secret. pii is redacted before the audit hash; secret is never stored.

title: Audit level
meaning: How much an audit record holds: metadata, or change with the before and after state. change is the default.

title: Resource type
meaning: The type an entity has in the authorization schema. Its permissions and relations are checked against the compiled schema.

title: Relationship
meaning: One tuple that relates a resource to a subject. Generated code and fills write one only through the outbox, never directly.

title: Idempotency key
meaning: The key a client sends with a create or an update, so a retry replays the stored response instead of acting again.

title: Ledger
meaning: An entity of kind ledger: accounts, transfers and entries in one currency, append-only and balanced.

title: Ledger account
meaning: One account of a ledger, with a normal balance of debit or credit and an optional minimum balance.

title: Normal balance
meaning: The side an account grows on: debit or credit.

title: Mode
meaning: A named component set the one binary runs: api, worker or controller. all runs every set and is the default.

title: Bound mixin
meaning: A mixin the declaration binds beside its archetype: a component set it adds, such as durable-events or kafka-events.

title: Controller
meaning: A reconciler the service runs in controller mode, one active instance at a time under a lease with a fencing token.

title: Declared invariant
meaning: A rule across rows stated in the declaration with one of three kinds, each emitted as a database constraint.

title: Reason
meaning: The sentence a declaration gives when it leaves a default: tenancy kind single or audit off. The fleet shows it.

title: Component digest
meaning: The SHA-256 digest of one component's content in the registry. It changes only when that component's content changes.

title: Supersession
meaning: A statement that a component digest has a successor, with the date after which the old digest fails, and whether taking the successor needs a declaration or fill change.

title: Successor
meaning: The component digest that replaces a superseded digest. A platform engineer declares it. STEGO never infers it.

title: Withdrawal
meaning: A statement that a component digest must not be used any more, with the future date after which it fails.

title: Fail date
meaning: The date after which a superseded or withdrawn pin fails validation, and apply writes nothing.

title: Fleet
meaning: Every service whose record a sweep can read, in the checkouts a platform engineer names.

title: Compiler release
meaning: One signed compiler, built at one exact commit, that holds every generator STEGO can run.

title: Qualification
meaning: The check that the CI runs, required jobs and signed artifacts of a compiler release all passed at its exact commit.

title: Build identity
meaning: What the compiler records about its own build: its Go version, platform, module version, revision and source state.

title: Qualified platform
meaning: The one platform a compiler release is qualified for: Linux amd64.

title: Runtime version
meaning: One tagged version of the runtime library; it is superseded and withdrawn like a component digest, and the fleet sweep names every service on it.

title: Advisory
meaning: One OSV record in the registry that states a supersession or a withdrawal of a component digest, a runtime library version or a declaration version: its id, a summary, the affected package with its ranges and versions, a withdrawn timestamp when withdrawn, and references. STEGO's own fields, the successor digest, the fail date, and whether taking the successor needs a declaration or fill change, sit under database_specific.

title: VEX statement
meaning: One OpenVEX statement the fleet sweep emits for one service and one advisory, with the status affected, fixed or not_affected, so a consumer of the service reads the advisory's effect on it without reading the records.

title: platform-requirements.yaml
meaning: The typed file every service writes that states what its environment must supply, and holds no environment values.

title: Environment file
meaning: The platform's typed file for one service in one environment, kept in a platform-owned repo, that supplies every value the requirements name.

title: Kubernetes base
meaning: The plain kustomize base STEGO writes; the platform's overlay builds on it.

title: Overlay
meaning: The platform's kustomize layer for one environment: image digest, namespace, replicas, PodDisruptionBudget and resource changes.

title: Delivery object
meaning: The object a GitOps tool reads to deliver a service; an Argo CD Application for now.

title: Delivery candidate
meaning: An image a CI provider built, before every STEGO check has passed on it.

title: Trusted signer
meaning: The one identity a CI provider's images may be signed by: a pinned workflow's keyless identity, or a Tekton Chains key.

title: Fill
meaning: Hand-written code in a service's fills/ folder that implements one slot's contract for one collection, with its own tests.

title: Test evidence
meaning: The record in fill.yaml that a fill's tests passed against one exact state of the fill and its slot contract.

title: Sign-off
meaning: A person's key signature, in fill.yaml, of a fill's test evidence.

title: SIGNERS
meaning: The file named SIGNERS at the project root, like OWNERS, that lists the keys whose signatures may qualify a fill: SSH keys in the allowed signers format git uses, and GPG keys. Adding a signer is a reviewed change to it.

title: Qualified fill
meaning: A fill whose evidence matches its current code and contract, and whose evidence a listed key signed.

title: Fill module
meaning: A module that the declaration lets fills import, besides their contracts and the standard library.

title: Record
meaning: The part of .stego/state.yaml that says what a service's generated code was built from: the service, the compiler build, the registry content, every component pin and the hash of every generated file.

title: Component pin
meaning: The version and digest of one component that a service is built from.

title: Drift
meaning: A difference between a generated file and the hash its record holds, or between a recorded input and the file on disk.

title: Hand edit
meaning: A change to a generated file that no generation run made.

title: Journal
meaning: The file .stego/transaction.yaml. It holds an apply in progress, so recovery can complete it.

title: Saved plan
meaning: A plan that stego plan saved under .stego/, which apply carries out exactly. It is local, never committed.

title: Assembler
meaning: The part of the compiler that combines every generator's wiring into the service's entry point and module file.

title: Output namespace
meaning: The folder, in the output, that one component's generator may write to. No two components share one.

title: Architecture view
meaning: The self-contained HTML file every run writes that shows how a service is shaped and how it works, derived from the same inputs as its code.

title: Build-time binding
meaning: The rule that a service's declaration is turned into behavior when the code is generated, never at startup or per request; it is what makes a generated decision non-negotiable.

title: Declaration version
meaning: The version of the declaration format that a declaration states. The registry declares the versions it accepts; a breaking compiler release supersedes an old version through the registry's advisories, with a fail date; and stego fix rewrites a declaration to the next version where it can.

title: Mode registry
meaning: The table in the runtime that maps each mode name to its component set, which the entry point reads to start the modes the flag selects.

title: Component set
meaning: The named group of components one mode runs, with its own readiness and shutdown sequence. A mode is never a fixed bundle.

title: Registry
meaning: The set of archetypes, components and mixins that services are built from, pinned by one reference for each source.

title: Common registry
meaning: The reviewed registry every team trusts. A local registry may add to it, and may not replace a part of it.

title: Local registry
meaning: A registry that adds a team's own parts to the common registry.

title: Active registry
meaning: The one set of parts that the common registry and its local registries compose to.

title: Component
meaning: A deterministic generator with its config schema, ports, slots and output contracts, versioned and staged as one unit.

title: Archetype
meaning: A curated component set with its conventions: the golden path a service selects.

title: Mixin
meaning: An addition to an archetype that brings further components and slots, and replaces nothing.

title: Active component set
meaning: The components one service is built from: its archetype's components, those its mixins add, and the providers its declaration selects.

title: Port
meaning: A named contract between components. One component provides it, and others require it.

title: Provider
meaning: The component that answers a port in an active component set.

title: Slot
meaning: A typed extension point a component declares, where a service binds its own rules as fills.

title: Namespace
meaning: The output path a component may write into.

title: Maturity stage
meaning: Where a component is on the ladder alpha, beta, ga.

title: Sunset
meaning: The date an alpha or beta component stops working.

title: Golden path
meaning: The shape an archetype gives a service, which holds only ga components.

title: Output contract
meaning: One fact that must always hold of the code a component emits. The component owns it, not the service.

title: Generator
meaning: A file of a component's generator that emits part of the component's code.

title: Quality bar
meaning: What a component version must hold to be ga: a security review, a benchmark against a reference and a design review, each at its exact digest, a reference comparison of its contract set at that set's digest, and a pass of the conformance tests of each port it provides, at its digest.

title: Promotion
meaning: Moving a component from a team's local registry into the common registry, through review, so every team can build from it.

title: Architecture role
meaning: A component's stated layer, part in a request flow and port sides, from which the architecture view places it.

title: Runtime library
meaning: The one versioned Go module that holds the code every service shares and no declaration changes, such as the outbox queue, the controller loop and tracing; generated code imports it at the version its archetype pins.

title: Static file
meaning: A file a component emits that comes out the same for every declaration; it belongs in the runtime library, and the registry refuses a component that emits one.

title: Framework
meaning: A dependency that inverts control: it scans, discovers or registers code by name, struct tag or init(), or interprets the declaration at run time. A pinned library with a stable API that the service's own code calls is not one.

title: Reference comparison
meaning: The evidence that a component's promises are best of breed: each promise its best-in-field references make, adopted as a contract or declined with a reason, recorded at the contract set's digest.

title: Best-in-field reference
meaning: An implementation, library or standard that the field regards as the best solution to the problem a component solves; a component names one or more, or states why none exists.

title: Promise list
meaning: A component's output contracts read as what a service owner may rely on; written from the outcome and the references before the generator, never from the code.

title: Allocation profile
meaning: A fixed shape for a namespace a service hands out: its prefix, quota, accounts, bindings, identity seal, network isolation and Pod rules. The declaration gives the values; the namespace-allocation component gives the mechanism.

title: Allocated namespace
meaning: A namespace the allocator created from a profile for one owner on a shared cluster; it is marked, sealed, bounded and released as a whole.

title: Control namespace
meaning: The namespace that holds the allocator worker and the fixed control accounts; what runs in an allocated namespace never reaches it.
